name: Amariah
overview: Amariah was a male Aaronic priest from the tribe of Levi, noted in the book of Nehemiah. He is specifically mentioned among the leaders who sealed the covenant document in Nehemiah 10:3, highlighting his role in the religious reforms during that period. His priestly service underscores his importance in maintaining the spiritual heritage of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Amariah means 'Yahweh has said,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's authority. This proper name, as recorded in Nehemiah 10:3, connects the individual to divine communication or command, fitting for a priestly figure.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Jehohanan as Amariah's father, an inference drawn from Nehemiah 12:13. Beyond this paternal relationship, no additional family connections are recorded for Amariah in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Amariah's significance lies in his role as an Aaronic priest who actively participated in the covenant renewal under Nehemiah's leadership. Being named on the sealed document in Nehemiah 10 signifies his commitment to uphold God's law and support the communal return to faithful worship. His presence affirms the continuity of the Levitical priesthood in guiding Israel's spiritual restoration.
